rows.note: Found 2026-08-28 by T4(b) on the numeric/leading-zero axis, after the rulings landed. The disagreement was NOT about the numeric domain (R6 settles that) but about what an engine owes when its PARSER refuses the source. RULED the same day: it does not refuse. A source the parser rejects is a NON-CANDIDATE, and a non-candidate is silent — the same shape R4 gives an over-deep spine. A refusal is a claim about a program, and an unparseable source is not a program to make claims about. Both legs now enforce this at their own parse boundary, each asking its OWN parser: ck checks parseDiagnostics, the oxc surface checks parseSync errors, and the oxlint surface never runs a rule over a file it could not parse. Boundary evidence: of the numeric forms, `0_1` alone is a parse error for BOTH parsers — 1_000, 0x1f, 1.5 and 1n all parse cleanly and stay R6 refusals; and none of the 265 fixtures carries a parse diagnostic, so the gate is untouched.

rows.varied: import type * as Effect (type-only, erased at compile time)
rows.note: Both engines AGREE, and the agreement is the defect: a type-only import is erased, so at runtime `Effect.gen` is a ReferenceError and the recognized program cannot execute. The hoover leg hands the Lean execute leg instructions for a program that does not run. R3 declared this admissible ('import type bindings still count -- the recognizer is syntax-only and type-blind, symmetric on both legs'), but declaring a deviation does not discharge it. The gate cannot see this: two type-blind engines agreeing proves only that they read syntax the same way, and N-version agreement is worth nothing against a fault in the shared blind spot.

oracle.mechanism: transformSync(file, src, { typescript: { onlyRemoveTypeImports: true } }) -- the verbatimModuleSyntax semantics. An import that does not appear in the emitted code does not exist at runtime.
oracle.evidence: Under onlyRemoveTypeImports:true the erasure is exact and PER-SPECIFIER: `import type * as Effect` and `import type { gen }` are erased; `import { type gen, pipe }` keeps `pipe` and drops `gen`; value imports survive even when unused or used only in type position. Under the default (false) elision is USAGE-dependent -- `import { gen }` vanishes merely because the body calls `Effect.gen` -- which would make the oracle depend on the candidate it is judging.
oracle.seam: transformSync is synchronous, so this fits `recognize : SourceText -> Verdict[]` with no change to the engine seam.
oracle.scope: Closes IMPORT SURVIVAL only. It still cannot tell that `store` is a Store, or that `hex` is the pinned helper -- Rule 7 stays disabled and every lift still carries helperUnpinned: true.
